sources.title: Mihalis Dafermos and Igor Rodnianski, Lectures on black holes and linear waves, arXiv:0811.0354v1 (2008)
sources.locator: Sections 3.2.2 and 3.2.4 (PDF pp. 30–32), §7.1 (PDF pp. 86–87), and Appendix F.2 (PDF pp. 105–106); complete relevant sections inspected.

contents.name: §3.2.2: The current J^T and its energy estimate
contents.support: The local lemma proves the potential/source divergence identity and its Killing-current specialization from the stated wave equation; the lecture-note current motivates the convention.

contents.name: §3.2.4: Degeneration at the horizon
contents.support: The local RN scalar result computes the exact radial energy coefficient f and proves its loss of control at the nonextremal horizon; no Schwarzschild estimate is transferred.

contents.name: §7.1: A general construction of vector fields Y and N
contents.support: The red-shift method requires a nondegenerate horizon estimate; the RN item explicitly says its conserved static energy is degenerate and supplies no red-shift conclusion.

contents.name: Appendix F.2: Regge-Wheeler coordinates (r*, t)
contents.support: The RN item defines a tortoise coordinate and derives the charged separated scalar equation directly from the RN metric rather than importing the Schwarzschild radial equation.

sources.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner-Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020)
sources.locator: §§1.2–1.3 (PDF pp. 3–6), §8.1.2 (PDF pp. 56–57), and §8.4 (PDF pp. 59–60); complete relevant sections inspected.

contents.name: §1.2: The gauge-invariant quantities and the Teukolsky system
contents.support: This coupled gravitational/electromagnetic system is retained as a scope caveat: the local result concerns a test scalar on a fixed RN metric and does not identify it with the coupled variables.

contents.name: §1.3: New feature in Reissner-Nordström: the projection to l=1 spherical harmonics
contents.support: The local result is conditional on a supplied scalar spherical harmonic and does not claim to resolve the distinct coupled Einstein-Maxwell low-mode sectors described in this section.

contents.name: §8.1.2: Generalized Regge-Wheeler system
contents.support: The source's actual coupled system has derivative couplings and lower-order forcing; the abstract symmetric nonnegative matrix-potential theorem deliberately assumes a different exact system.

contents.name: §8.4: Relation to the gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations of Reissner-Nordström spacetime
contents.support: The theorem's remarks preserve the need to derive exact coupled variables, low modes, and reconstruction before applying an abstract energy estimate.

sources.title: Mihalis Dafermos and Igor Rodnianski, Lectures on black holes and linear waves, arXiv:0811.0354v1 (2008)
sources.locator: Appendix D (PDF pp. 103–104) and §3.2.2 (PDF pp. 30–31); complete relevant sections inspected.

contents.name: Appendix D: Vector field multipliers and their currents
contents.support: The counterexample uses this stress-current convention only to compare scope with the positive-potential theorem; its negative eigenfunction and growing solution are verified locally.

sources.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner-Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020)
sources.locator: §§1.2–1.4 (PDF pp. 3–7) and §8.1.2 (PDF pp. 56–57); complete relevant sections inspected.

contents.name: §1.2: The gauge-invariant quantities and the Teukolsky system
contents.support: The example explicitly limits its counterexample to arbitrary symmetric matrix potentials and disclaims any claim about actual Einstein-Maxwell master potentials.

contents.name: §1.4: Choice of gauge
contents.reason: The B item is a one-dimensional abstract potential counterexample, so the paper's Bondi-gauge conditions and reconstruction framework do not enter its construction.

contents.name: §8.1.2: Generalized Regge-Wheeler system
contents.support: This coupled system is context for the explicit limitation that the negative scalar potential is not asserted to be an Einstein-Maxwell master potential.
